館.meaning: On the left, a plate of <part>food</part>. On the right, a <part>bureaucrat</part> sits at his desk under a roof, stamping papers for every floor. Dinner by the door and offices piled on offices: it's a huge <kanji>building</kanji>, a mansion with its own kitchen.
館.on: Every room in the mansion has a single <sound>car</sound>nation in a vase.
館.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>!' you shout in the hall, and a <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of a marble <sound>tu</sound>b.

夜.meaning: Someone puts a <part>lid</part> on the <part>evening</part> like a pot, and the last light goes out. You hang your coat on the <part>coat hook</part>, and outside the moon is the only lamp left. It's <kanji>night</kanji>.
夜.on: In the dark, the cat finds a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn and unwinds it all over the house.
夜.kun: Half asleep, you eat a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt by moonlight while a kanga<sound>roo</sound> snores under the coat hook.

米.meaning: A cross in the middle, with four little strokes flying off its corners. Someone has dropped a sack, and the grains have bounced out from the center in every direction. Sweep them up and cook them: <kanji>rice</kanji>.
米.on: The sack falls off a boat into the <sound>bay</sound>, and grains float all over the water.
米.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala eats the rice off a <sound>me</sound>tal plate, one grain at a time.

来.meaning: A plank lies on top of a heap of <part>rice</part>, like a sign over a market stall. A single grain falls off, and every pigeon in the city hears it. Wings everywhere: drop rice, and the birds will <kanji>come</kanji>.
来.on: Then a <sound>rhi</sound>no smells the rice and comes too, and the pigeons scatter.
来.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> come running for the rice as well.

茶.meaning: Under a hat of <part>grass</part>, a <part>person</part> stoops over a small <part>tree</part>, picking its leaves one by one. She dries them in the sun and pours hot water over them. The cup turns green: <kanji>tea</kanji>.
茶.on: After two cups of tea, Grandma gets up and dances the <sound>cha</sound>-cha.

面.meaning: A flat bar like a headband, and under it a big box with an eye-shaped box inside. It's a face with no expression at all, painted on wood and tied on with string. Put it on and nobody knows who you are: a <kanji>mask</kanji>.
面.on: At the café, the waiter in the mask hands you a <sound>men</sound>u and won't say a word.
面.kun: You lift the mask. '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a <sound>mo</sound>le, and a <sound>te</sound>nor sings to your bare face.
